citations.verbatim_statement: The complete source carrier is as follows, with the source definitions faithfully paraphrased and its theorem notation preserved. Maintained Assumption~3.5 requires well-defined binary potential outcomes depending only on the unit's own assignment and consistency \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)=A_tY_t(1)+(1-A_t)Y_t(0)\) almost surely. Assumption~3.6 requires the triples \((X_t,Y_t(0),Y_t(1))\) to be independent across \(t\) and identically distributed, with a generic superpopulation draw unaffected by the adaptive policy. Assumption~3.2 requires the logged executed propensity \(\pi_t\) to be \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable, to lie in \((0,1)\), and to equal the probability used by the randomization device, so \(P(A_t=1\mid\mathcal G_t)=\pi_t\) almost surely. Assumption~3.7 requires \(A_t\) to be conditionally independent of \((Y_t(0),Y_t(1))\) given the pre-treatment sigma-field \(\mathcal G_t\). Assumption~3.8 requires one \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every scored index obeys \(\varepsilon\le\pi_t\le1-\varepsilon\) almost surely. Assumption~4.5 requires each scored nuisance regression \(\widehat m_{t-1,a}\) to be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and hence not to depend on the current treatment and outcome or on future data. Assumption~4.8 requires the scored set \(\mathcal T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) to be fixed before data collection. Assumption~3.9 requires \(E[|Y(a)|^4]<\infty\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Assumption~3.10 requires a finite \(C\) such that \(\sup_{n\ge1}\sup_{t\in\mathcal T}E[|\widehat m_{t-1,a}(X_t)|^4]\le C\) for each arm. Assumption~5.11 requires \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}:=|\mathcal T|\to\infty\) and some \(v_->0\) for which \(P(V_T^2\ge v_-n_{\mathrm{eff}})\to1\), where \(V_T^2\) is predictable quadratic variation; it does not require stabilization of \(V_T^2/n_{\mathrm{eff}}\). Under Assumptions~3.6, 3.2, 3.7, 3.8, 4.5, 4.8, 3.9, 3.10, and 5.11, Theorem~5.14 defines \(S_T=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}(\widehat\phi_t-\theta_0)\) and \(Q_T=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}(\widehat\phi_t-\theta_0)^2\), asserts \(S_T/\sqrt{Q_T}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) in equation~(5.5), asserts \(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{eff}}}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)/\widehat V^{1/2}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) in equation~(5.6), and consequently asserts asymptotically correct coverage for the Wald interval in equation~(4.7) at the prespecified horizon without deterministic variance stabilization.
